sections.html:
Rabun County counted 16,883 residents in 2020 and an estimated 17,764 in July 2025. The tax commissioner's office is in Clayton. With 370.13 land square miles and 45.6 residents per square mile, it is thinly settled, and the average commute is a short 23.1 minutes.

Owners live in 77.1% of housing. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $295,200, rent runs about $1,047, and the middle household income is $67,493. Owners with a mortgage pay $1,481 a month in housing costs, and owners without a loan pay $491. People 65 and older are 31.5% of residents.

The county has 12,695 housing units but only 7,615 households, so many properties are not a household's main residence. If yours is one of them, it may not hold a homestead exemption, and the next owner's bill could differ from the one you pay now. Price from nearby closed sales, not county averages, because the spread between a village lot and mountain acreage can be wide. Building permits numbered 128 in 2025.

sections.h2: Tax offices and how to pay
sections.html:
The tax commissioner is at 19 Jo Dotson Circle, Suite 101, Clayton, GA 30525, phone (706) 782-3613, with weekday counter hours that end at 4:30 pm, major holidays excluded.

Rabun County payment options
Payment methodCost
Online by card2.50% or a $1.25 minimum
Online by eCheck$1.50 each
Mail, check payable to the Rabun County Tax CommissionerNone listed

A cart lets you pay several bills at once online. The assessors handle values, returns, special programs and appeals, and copies of deeds come from the deed room at the Rabun County Courthouse.

Bills are mailed to whoever owns the property. A lender with an escrow account will not get one, so send yours along.

sections.h2: When is Rabun County property tax due, and what happens late?
sections.html:
December 1 applies to real estate and business personal property.

Past that date, prime plus 3% accrues monthly, and 120 days later a 5% penalty joins it. Once a bill is over 90 days late, a FIFA lien can be recorded, and the commissioner may levy on the parcel. The lien becomes a public record that credit bureaus may read.

The county accepts a United States Postal Service postmark, not a metered one. Mobile homes are billed in January. Call (706) 782-3613 for the due date before paying one.

sections.h2: How to contest a Rabun County value
sections.html:
File the appeal in writing, and file it early. An appeal filed late is invalid. The deadline is 45 days after the notice.

There are three grounds: whether the property is taxable or exempt, whether it is valued in line with comparable property, and whether the dollar value is too high or too low. The assessors review it, and if nothing changes, the Board of Equalization hears the case. Rabun County Superior Court is the next level for either side.

The assessors follow the market and do not create it, using cost, market and income approaches. A recent sale price of a similar nearby house gives the strongest backing.

Land owners have more choices here than house owners. Every program below ties the land to its use for 10 years by covenant. Apply between January 2 and April 1.

  • Preferential agricultural: taxed on 30% of fair market value where other property uses 40%.
  • Conservation use: current use value replaces market value.
  • Environmentally sensitive: land left in its natural state, valued by use if it meets Department of Natural Resources standards.
  • Residential transitional: current use value where an area is moving away from residential use.

Standing timber is taxed once it is sold or harvested. Anyone selling land under a covenant should tell buyers, since the 10-year commitment affects what they can do with it.

The test is ownership plus residence on January 1, and the form goes to the assessors. It must arrive before April 1 to count for that year. Call (706) 782-3613 if you are unsure which window applies to you.

Owners aged 62 can ask for an additional exemption. Arithmetic is simple: take 40% of market value, subtract exemptions, and apply the rate set by the county commissioners and the school board. The money pays for police, fire, schools, roads, bridges, water and parks.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Rabun County house with tax still owed?
sections.html:
Yes, with a payoff from the commissioner and the closing attorney handling it.

  1. Ask for the exact balance with interest and any penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA has been recorded.
  3. If the land is in a covenant program, share that with the buyer.
  4. List each payoff on the settlement statement.

A house stalled by repairs or long vacancy can sell as-is, on a closing day you choose, with the tax paid out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: Preparing a vacation or second home for sale
sections.html:
Because so many Rabun properties are not a household's main residence, check your tax status before you list. Ask the assessors whether a homestead exemption is on file. A buyer's estimate of next year's bill depends on it, and a surprise at closing can sour a deal.

Land with a covenant needs extra care. Tell the buyer which program applies and that the 10-year commitment runs with the land, then confirm with the assessors what the buyer must do to keep the program going. If the parcel mixes house and acreage, the two parts may be valued differently.

Before you call a buyer or an agent, collect the current bill, the payoff from the commissioner, and your deed copy from the courthouse deed room. A cash buyer can close on a vacant or stalled property without waiting for a lender's appraisal, and the tax is still paid at the table from your proceeds.

faqs.q: When do Rabun County property taxes come due?
faqs.a: December 1, for real estate and business personal property.

faqs.q: Where is the Rabun County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: At 19 Jo Dotson Circle, Suite 101, in Clayton. Call (706) 782-3613. Counter hours end at 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline in Rabun County?
faqs.a: The deadline is 45 days after the notice. A later appeal is invalid.

faqs.q: Can I pay Rabun County tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, online. The fee is 2.50% or $1.25 minimum for cards, and $1.50 for each eCheck.

faqs.q: Which Rabun County programs need a 10-year covenant?
faqs.a: Preferential agricultural, conservation use, environmentally sensitive and residential transitional assessments. Apply from January 2 to April 1.
